MAJOR: AC-1 tension: the delta makes the on-mode unlisted path open/write a file (`PF_BACKLOG_METRICS_FILE`) in `_raise_unlisted`, and `test_ac2_unlisted_metric_export` asserts that file write — contradicting AC-1 "instead of reading or writing files" and the design invariant "On + unlisted never touches files". Reconcile the contract (scope the invariant to backlog-authority files, or derive the counter from the existing structured log) so the shipped behavior and AC text agree.

Textfile counter semantics are not alert-grade: `_DB_UNLISTED_COUNT` is process-local, rewritten with mode `"w"` on every raise, so any second worker/instance sharing one path clobbers the value (count goes backwards) and restarts reset it; `increase(backlog_db_scope_unlisted_total[10m]) >= 3` then pages on noise or misses sustained failures. Needs monotonic, process-qualified export (or per-process metric names).

Design contract lists `config/env-flags.json` as an affected file, but neither the delta nor the full candidate registers the new `PF_BACKLOG_METRICS_FILE` switch, violating the env-flags registry discoverability standard and the approved design's file list.
MINOR: Alert annotation runbook points at `engineering/evidence/BI-PF-1534/operator-recovery.md` while all sibling alerts use `docs/BACKLOG-AUTHORITY-RUNBOOK.md`; evidence artifacts are review deliverables, not shipped ops docs, so oncall gets a dangling runbook link.

The alert has no coverage when `PF_BACKLOG_METRICS_FILE` is unset (series absent, no `absent()` guard), and `for: 10m` plus a 10m increase window yields ~20m lead time, weakening CL-014 alert lead-time.
`except Exception: pass` around the metric write silently drops observability with no log line, and the sync open/write happens on every repeated raise (unbounded I/O on a failure path).

`test_ac2_unlisted_metric_export` is tagged `-k ac2` but asserts only metric export, not AC-2's write/delete/ID fail-closed contract, so the AC-2 evidence command now matches a test that does not exercise AC-2.
NIT: Test uses chained `;`-separated one-liner `monkeypatch.setenv` calls, hard to read/diff and at odds with the Python style guide.
Test never asserts the negative side of fail-closed (no backlog item file created/touched), which would strengthen the AC-1 proof cheaply.
SUMMARY: The delta substantively resolves the prior observability MAJOR by adding a real exported counter and a sustained-failure alert, but introduces a contract conflict (file write on the very path AC-1 says must not touch files) and a non-monotonic, clobber-prone textfile counter that undermines the new page alert.

Top risks: multi-process counter clobbering/reset making `ProductForgeBacklogScopeUnlisted` unreliable, undeclared `PF_BACKLOG_METRICS_FILE` flag, and alert runbook pointing at ephemeral evidence rather than shipped ops docs.
